pull.title: KAFKA-21302:  Sort copartition groups and indexes for consistent Streams topology comparison
pull.body:
Fixes KAFKA-21302

With `group.protocol=streams`, a member with identical copartition
constraints can be rejected because of differences in source topic
ordering. For example, constructing the same join with source topics
`["A", "B"]` and `["B", "A"]` can produce heartbeat copartition indexes
of `[0, 1, 2]` and `[1, 0, 2]`, respectively.

The coordinator compares these lists in an order-sensitive manner and
treats the second member’s request as a topology change. It returns
`INVALID_REQUEST`, causing the client to transition to FATAL and
preventing an otherwise valid instance from joining or replacing an
existing member

Reviewers: Lucas Brutschy <lbrutschy@confluent.io>

repo.name: kafka
repo.description: Apache Kafka - A distributed event streaming platform

reviews.body:
### 🟢 Approval recommended Normalization preserves index targets and inputs, with focused regression coverage and no unresolved findings. **No open issues** 🎉
What changed in this PR Makes Streams topology comparison insensitive to copartition group and index ordering, preventing rejection of members with equivalent constraints. **Changes:** - Normalizes copartition constraints during record replay and heartbeat processing without changing referenced topic lists. - Adds regression coverage for equality, input preservation, and successful member joins. | File | Description | | ---- | ----------- | | group-coordinator/​src/​test/​java/​org/​apache/​kafka/​coordinator/​group/​streams/​StreamsTopologyTest.java | Tests normalization, equality, and input preservation. | | group-coordinator/​src/​test/​java/​org/​apache/​kafka/​coordinator/​group/​GroupMetadataManagerTest.java | Verifies joins with reordered copartition constraints succeed. | | group-coordinator/​src/​main/​java/​org/​apache/​kafka/​coordinator/​group/​streams/​StreamsTopology.java | Normalizes copartition groups and indexes across both ingestion paths. |
Review effort: Balanced

### 🟡 Changes recommended Only the request side is sorted during matching, so topologies built from unsorted input can fail to match themselves; normalization must cover all construction paths or both comparison sides, with an unsorted self-match regression test.
1 open issue - [Normalize StreamsTopology ordering across all construction paths](https://github.com/apache/kafka/pull/23855#discussion_r4411202776) · New
Review effort: Balanced

review_comments.body: Could we also cover a group that mixes source and repartition indexes, e.g. `{source: [1], repartition: [0]}`? That's the typical join case, and it's where the `thenComparing` tie-breaks actually matter.
Maybe also assert that `result.records()` contains no new topology record, so we know the request was matched against the existing topology?

This deep-copies the whole subtopology, including all the TopicInfos and their configs, just to sort the copartition groups, and `fromHeartbeatRequest` now copies twice (convert + duplicate). Could we only copy the copartition groups? If we sort in `convertToStreamsGroupTopologyRecord` as suggested in the review body, the heartbeat path doesn't need a copy at all.

Also, `convertToTopicInfo` maps a null `topicConfigs` to null, and `duplicate()` would NPE on that. A deserialized request can't have null there since the field isn't nullable, so maybe that null branch is just dead code. But it's another reason not to duplicate fields we don't touch.

nit: this is a hand-rolled lexicographic compare. Not a big deal, but since the lists are sorted at this point, would something like converting to `short[]` and using `Arrays.compare` be simpler? Fine to keep as is if you prefer.

Thinking about this more: since the join heartbeat can be hot on large clusters (e.g. during rejoin storms), could we avoid building a `StreamsTopology` from the request at all when the group already has one? `maybeUpdateTopology` already converts the full request on every topology-carrying heartbeat, and with the normalization we copy it a second time.

One option: only call `fromHeartbeatRequest` when initializing the topology, and otherwise compare the request directly against the stored topology with something like `StreamsTopology#matches(StreamsGroupHeartbeatRequestData.Topology)`, matching copartition groups regardless of order. The stored topology is already normalized in `fromRecord`, and the groups are tiny, so this can be done without allocating. It would need a test that fails when a field is added to `Subtopology`, so the comparison doesn't silently miss it. I'd rather not override `equals` for this, since `hashCode` would also need to be made order-independent.

What do you think?

@lucasbru 

Thank you for the thoughtful suggestion. I agree that, considering cases such as rejoin storms, optimizing this path with `matches()` is important for the broker.

Would you be open to first applying your initial suggestion to copy only the copartition groups, then landing and backporting the correctness fix before moving on to `matches()`? (I'm happy to take on the `matches()` optimization separately.)

My concern is that introducing a new comparison implementation covering the current schema could inadvertently introduce new correctness issues. With that in mind, I would prefer to keep this PR narrowly focused on handling the ordering differences between client requests and the broker’s stored topology, and complete the backports first(even client side!).

If you’re comfortable with that approach, could we address the `matches()` optimization in a separate ticket, with dedicated review and testing, including the schema field-coverage test you suggested?

I think `matches()` would actually replace the normalization rather than add to it: with an order-insensitive comparison we don't need to sort or copy the copartition groups at all, and `fromRecord`/`fromHeartbeatRequest` stay as they were. The current version also lists the `Subtopology` fields explicitly, so the risk of missing a field is the same either way and needs the same reflection test. So I'd lean towards doing it in this PR. What do you think?
Sorry, my nit made this slightly worse: `toArray(Short[]::new)` allocates two arrays on every comparison. The previous loop didn't allocate, so if we keep the normalization I'd go back to it.

Since this lists the fields explicitly, a field added to `Subtopology` later (it would have to be a tagged field) would be silently dropped here. Could we add a small test that counts the declared instance fields of `StreamsGroupTopologyValue.Subtopology` via reflection (8 today, including `_unknownTaggedFields`)? A schema field count wouldn't catch tagged fields. Or at least a comment saying this has to list every field. The same applies to `matches()` if we go that way.

Yes, you are right! 
I've addressed it.

Definitely agree. 
I think this is an area where regressions could easily be introduced if new fields are added in the future.

Thanks for doing this, and sorry, my "without allocating" comment pushed in this direction. When the order differs, `sameTopicIndexes` is O(k²) and `matchesCopartitionGroups` O(G²), and nothing bounds those sizes in the request. A client with access to the group can initialize it with a large index list (~100KB already gives ~10⁹ iterations) and then rejoin with a permutation, which keeps the coordinator thread busy on every such heartbeat.

I think sorting is both simpler and safe here: in `fromRecord`, `duplicate()` the subtopology and sort its copartition groups (indexes within each group, then the groups, with the old allocation-free `compareTopicIndexes` loop). This only runs on initialization and load, and it needs to be a copy because the handler passes the same `recordValue` it is about to write, and the lists are unmodifiable or shared with the request. `fromHeartbeatRequest` should then delegate to `fromRecord` again. In `matches`, sort copies of just the request's copartition groups and compare them with the stored ones. That's O(k log k), records stay as the client sent them, and the counting code goes away.
This is O(S²) in the number of subtopologies, with S only bounded by the record size (~1e5 minimal subtopologies). Could we track the seen IDs in a `HashSet` instead?

Since `matches` now compares every field by hand, could we add one parameterized test that changes a single non-copartition field at a time and asserts `matches` is false: source topics, sink topics, a changelog/repartition `TopicInfo` field (partitions, replication factor, configs), a missing subtopology, a duplicate subtopology ID? Otherwise a wrong comparison of an existing field would go unnoticed, and the field-count test only covers new fields.
nit: `current` was looked up by `requested.subtopologyId()` in a map keyed by subtopology ID, so this check is always true. I'd drop it.

I agree. 
In that case, performance degradation is expected. 
I've addressed it!

Thanks for your suggestion. it is much better. 
I've addressed it.

One more things I want to say is that `matches()` will return `false` if the request contains duplicate subtopology IDs. This prevents a request from matching the same stored subtopology multiple times while omitting another.
I've added another parameterized test!

`current` is not necessarily sorted: `StreamsTopology.fromHeartbeatRequest(...)` and the public constructors still preserve the supplied ordering. For example, with a copartition group containing `[1, 0]`, `StreamsTopology.fromHeartbeatRequest(request).matches(request)` returns false because only the request side is sorted to `[0, 1]`. Please enforce normalization on every construction path or normalize both sides here, and add a self-match regression test using an unsorted request.

`fromHeartbeatRequest()` is currently only used in tests. Both production initialization and replay go through `fromRecord()`, which normalizes copartition groups before `matches()` is called. The self-match inconsistency exists, but it does not affect the current production path.

issue_comments.body:
Thanks for the fix! I think we should also fix this on the client. `StreamsGroupHeartbeatRequestManager#getCopartitionGroupsFromStreams` builds the index lists and the list of groups by iterating a `Set`, which is where the nondeterministic order comes from. Could you sort the indexes within each group and then the groups there too, the same way we already sort source/sink/repartition topics in `fromStreamsToHeartbeatRequest`? Clients would then always send a canonical topology. We'd still keep the broker-side normalization permanently, both on join and on replay, because of older clients and already-persisted unsorted records. A test in `StreamsGroupHeartbeatRequestManagerTest` that checks the sorted output would be good too.

It might also be worth sorting in `convertToStreamsGroupTopologyRecord`, so that newly written topology records are canonical too. The record format doesn't change, and it means a broker downgrade won't reject newer, sorted clients against a stored record. `fromRecord` would still normalize for groups created before this change.

@lucasbru 
Thanks for taking the time to review! 

I agree that we should fix the client side as well. Given the backport implications, would it make sense to track that change in a separate ticket and PR?

AFAIK, Copartition groups are persisted, including their ordering. If an existing client is upgraded to send sorted groups while the broker remains unpatched, the broker could reject the topology because its ordering differs from the persisted record, even though the topology is semantically unchanged.

Separating the client-side change would let us backport the broker normalization independently and evaluate the client-side backport with this compatibility concern in mind.

What do you think?

Good point, I hadn't thought about the unpatched-broker case. Agreed, let's keep this PR broker-only so it can be backported on its own, and handle the client side in a separate ticket.

The same argument applies to my suggestion of writing sorted records: if a patched broker writes sorted records and is later downgraded, existing clients sending the old order would be rejected. So let's drop that and keep persisting what the client sent.

Thanks for the clarification! 
First of all, I've created new ticket for client side. (https://issues.apache.org/jira/browse/KAFKA-21320)

Currently, I'm working on addressing your comments in this PR.
I'll be back ASAP with new commit!

Small addition after looking at how the client builds the groups: the order comes from `HashSet` iteration in `InternalTopologyBuilder#copartitionGroups`, which is deterministic for the same topology code. So instances running the same code always send the same order, and the mismatch only happens when equivalent topologies are written differently (e.g. join order swapped) and the topic names collide in the same hash bucket.

That also means existing records generally match what current clients send, which makes your point about sorting on the client even stronger. A sorting client would usually differ from the persisted order on an unpatched broker.

@lucasbru 

I've pushed a new commit that incorporates most of your suggestions!

I left out the `matches()` optimization for now, as I think it would be better to address it in a separate issue. However, if you consider it a minor change, I'm also happy to include it in this PR. Just let me know what you think!

I also added a comment at the end of KAFKA-21302. Even when running the exact same code, the ordering of copartition groups can vary across JVM runs if the source nodes are defined using `Set.of(...)`.

I wanted to highlight this again, as I thought it might be helpful when determining the priority of this issue.

When you get a chance, please take another look! 🙇‍♂️
Thanks for the update and for checking the `Set.of` case, you are right. This can happen without code changes, in some cases (more detail in the ticket).

@lucasbru 
Thanks for taking the time to review this carefully! 
I reverted change for the normalization and implemented matches method and some test cases.
When you get a chance, please take another look. 🙇‍♂️

@lucasbru 
Sorry for the delay and thanks for taking time to look into this again!
I've addressed it based on your comments. 
When you get a chance, please take another look! 

Also, I've noticed that`₩StreamsTopology.fromHeartbeatRequest()` is only used in tests.
If this new commit looks good to you, I'll create a follow-up commit to remove its usage from the tests.
